claim: Berlin's Computerspielemuseum (Karl-Marx-Allee 93A) covers gaming culture since the 1950s with 300+ exhibits and a playable retro arcade, open daily 10:00-20:00, admission EUR 12 / 8 reduced in 2026.
quote: With over 300 exhibits, the Computerspielemuseum is all about gaming culture and its development since the early 1950s. The museum is open daily from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

claim: Berlin's DDR Museum is an interactive East-German daily-life museum (sit in a Trabi, recreated GDR apartment, simulated Stasi surveillance), open daily 09:00-21:00, admission EUR 13.90 / 8.50 reduced.
quote: the museum is open seven days a week and on public holidays... 09:00-21:00 daily

claim: Berlin's Deutsches Currywurst Museum has been permanently closed since 21 December 2018 and is not operating in 2026 despite still appearing on many listings.
quote: The Deutsches Currywurst Museum has been permanently closed since 21 December 2018.

claim: Berlin clusters several offbeat single-theme museums including the Museum of Things (Werkbundarchiv), the DesignPanoptikum and spycraft museums alongside the Computerspielemuseum.
quote: Technology and design are presented in the DesignPanoptikum, Werkbundarchiv (Museum of Things) and at the Computerspielemuseum.

claim: Vienna's Funeral Museum (Bestattungsmuseum) at the Central Cemetery exhibits a reusable trapdoor coffin and 'save-yourself' bells against premature burial; open Wed-Fri 10:00-16:00, admission EUR 9.
quote: Address: Simmeringer Hauptstraße 234, Tor 2, 1110 Wien... Hours: Wed-Fri 10:00-16:00... Admission: EUR 9

claim: Vienna's Globe Museum (Palais Mollard) is the world's only public globe museum with 240 Earth, celestial, lunar and Mars globes; open Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, EUR 6 combined ticket with the Esperanto Museum.
quote: Presents 240 original Earth, celestial, lunar, and Mars globes... Hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; Thu until 21:00... Admission: EUR 6 combined with Esperanto Museum

claim: Vienna's Esperanto Museum, in the same Palais Mollard building, is one of the world's oldest language museums and documents over 500 constructed languages; Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, EUR 6 combined ticket.
quote: One of the world's oldest language museums; explores over 100 years of Esperanto's multifaceted history... Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00

claim: Vienna's deep bench of quirky museums also includes the Snow Globe Museum (Perzy family, inventors of the Viennese snow globe), the Third Man Museum (2,500 film exhibits, open Sat only) and the Clock Museum (700 working clocks).
quote: The Perzy family has manufactured original Viennese snow globes since the late 19th century... Third Man Museum... contains 2,500 exhibits including film props and Anton Karas's famous zither... Clock Museum... nearly 700 working clocks

claim: Munich's Deutsches Jagd- und Fischereimuseum, in a former church on Neuhauser Strasse, is famous for displays of Wolpertingers, mythical Bavarian taxidermy-hybrid creatures; entry around EUR 5, cash only.
quote: small natural history museum in Munich's city center and features legendary wolpertingers. As of 2024, the entrance fee is 5 euros and they only accept cash

claim: Munich offbeat picks include the Valentin-Karlstadt-Musaeum (comedy museum in the Isartor tower honoring Karl Valentin), the Munich Toy Museum (four floors in the Old Town Hall tower) and the city's potato museum.
quote: The Toy Museum in the Old Town Hall spans four floors with a narrow winding staircase... The Potato Museum in Munich is one of three potato museums in the country

claim: Zurich's Moulagenmuseum at the University of Zurich holds one of the world's largest collections of lifelike wax casts of skin diseases and injuries (leprous noses, eye ulcers, ear abscesses).
quote: The Museum of Wax Moulage at the University of Zurich features incredibly lifelike wax casts of skin diseases or injuries, including noses with leprosy, eye ulcers, and ear abscesses in life-size realism.

claim: Switzerland's weirdest museums include Zurich's Wax Moulage museum, Basel's Spielzeug Welten Museum (2,500 teddy bears, world's largest such collection) and the Henkermuseum hangman/torture museum in Sissach near Basel.
quote: The Spielzeug Welten Museum Basel (Toy Worlds Museum Basel) has 2,500 teddy bears, the largest collection in the world... The Henkermuseum (Hangman's Museum) in Sissach... crammed with instruments of execution and torture

claim: Basel's Museum Tinguely houses the world's largest collection of Jean Tinguely's kinetic sculptures that whirr and move at the push of a button; open Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00 (Thu to 21:00), closed Mondays.
quote: Opening hours are Tuesday to Sunday 11 am to 6 pm, with extended hours until 9 pm on Thursdays; closed on Mondays. The museum houses the world's largest collection of works by Swiss artist Jean Tinguely.

claim: Hamburg's Miniatur Wunderland in the Speicherstadt is the world's largest model railway with 1,100+ trains, 289,000 figures and a working miniature airport, peppered with thousands of hidden humorous scenes.
quote: More than 1,100 trains with over 10,000 wagons as well as 137,000 trees, 289,000 figures, 10,250 cars, 47 airplanes in the air, 16,138 meters of track... peppered the entire exhibition with thousands of humorous, quirky, and sometimes slightly risqué scenes

claim: Hamburg's Spicy's Gewuerzmuseum in the Speicherstadt is a smell-touch-taste spice museum with 900+ exhibits across five centuries and free entry, making a quick offbeat half-hour stop.
quote: A museum to smell, touch and taste – with over 900 exhibits spanning five centuries... Free entry makes it a low-cost highlight.
